text:
Rasmus Dahlin is off to a slower start than usual, as The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn put it, and the line agrees: 11 points in 17 games, about 1.57 per 60 against 2.38 last season. Buffalo plays him 24:39 a night and he is still the engine. The Sabres take 54.1% of shot attempts and 51.53% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on, and they are better with him than without.

The quiet start is mostly the team around him. With Dahlin on the ice, the Sabres have scored about as many goals as their chances deserve, and his own finishing is right on track, so this looks more like a quiet month than a decline. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 99th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 12th among defensemen in wins above replacement, so the creation tends to show up eventually.

Buffalo has won two of its last seven, a run that includes an 8-3 loss to Tampa Bay and a 2-0 loss in Dallas. Whatever turns that around probably runs through the former first overall pick.
headline: Rasmus Dahlin, still driving, not yet scoring
